label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L >= 8)
explanation: Fires at the delimiter step, where the model emits the first original token, almost exclusively when the sequence is long. The <DEL> step carries 86% of activation mass. The rate there climbs with L: none at L<=4, about 1% of steps at L=6, 5% at L=8, 9% at L=9 (by t), and L=9 holds 64% of mass. A weaker tail fires on the next one or two copy steps (recall_idx 1-2, mostly the re-fed first token) of long sequences, and the unit is essentially silent on original-phase steps. Even within the <DEL> step with L>=8, only about 30-40% of sequences fire. Which ones do depends on content: first original tokens v, m, u, w, b raise the rate about 2x, and c, i, 0, x lower it. No simple token rule sharpens precision, so the content dependence looks distributed. Length (to_go 7-8) and being at <DEL> modulate both firing and magnitude.
